keyFindings.description: Round 2's required change, the architect's ruling applied to the notice: every detail is introduced with "The install log ended:", including the `no-install-root` report whose install never ran and whose detail is "no writable install root: …". One conditional, with a case holding both the log-ful and log-less wordings as the gate's four sentences now are.

Gate fails open on a backslash-escaped quote. `split_comment` tracks `"` and `'` but not `\`, so in `echo "a \" # b" && bunx biome check .` it closes the string at the escaped quote, reads the rest as a comment, and `judge` passes only the prefix to `offenders`. Reproduced at this head: the whole file passes, exit 0, no marker and no trace. The shell disagrees (`sh -c 'echo "a \" # b" && echo RAN'` prints both). Distinct from round 1's quoted-marker hole, which is fixed and verified; this one predates that fix in the same function and I did not name it then. Nothing in the tree is hidden by it today.

`rm -f "$marker"` runs before the `lock-timeout` branch, so a waiter whose `flock -w` expired — a run that held the lock for zero seconds and learned nothing about node_modules — deletes a marker the holder wrote under the lock, and every later role of the issue pays a full reinstall. The adjacent path of round 1's finding 4, which my own remedy under-specified: the fix correctly covered the waiter that gets the lock. Move the removal below the branch.

The OSError fix stopped one layer short of the walk: `sorted(stack.pop().iterdir())` is unguarded, so a directory with mode 000 ends the required lint job in a raw PermissionError naming no file. Reproduced at this head. Fails closed, so a developer-experience defect rather than a silent green; same shape round 1 asked to be removed for files, and my remedy named only read_text.

JUDGED_FENCES puts `console`, `terminal`, `shell-session`, `shellsession` and `sh-session` on the judged side, and every line of such a block is judged, so a pasted session's output line that names one of the four tools is reported as a command — in the one block type whose convention interleaves commands with output, and against this round's own stated reason for the narrowing. The gate already models the separator (`PROMPT`). No judged guide uses those labels today.

The info string is now an escape hatch of its own — a block labelled `text`, or with a label the gate does not know, is not judged, with no reason and no record — while an exemption marker with no reason is itself reported. Record it where the exemptions are tabled, so a relabelled block reads as a decision rather than an accident.

Sent to the architect as a decision rather than a requested change: the setup install now holds /usr/bin/flock on $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR for as long as LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET allows, while the daemon's plugin install waits installLockWait (RegistrationDeadline/3, 120 s at the defaults, plugins.go:139-141) on that same inode, twice, and then exits 1 and fails the launch. docs/kubernetes.md:2058-2062 derives that bound's headroom from five serialised 24 s plugin installs and no other holder. The remedies (cap the locked region, widen the daemon's bound, or accept and correct the derivation) touch daemon code outside this diff.

verified: Round 1's nine findings re-checked at this head, each by running the thing rather than reading the reply: the gate's three sentences now true of the lines they are printed for; both quoted-marker shapes reported; a dangling symlink named rather than a traceback; a ```text block no longer judged while ```bash and ```console are; --backend=copyfile, the re-check inside the lock, the per-run mktemp log and the no-install-root report present in the script; the three e2e prescriptions and the two remedy texts migrated. All nine threads answered and left resolved.
CI at code head 0a65d80a: 25 check runs, all success or skipped, the required lint, typecheck, test and pr-title among them; compare 0a65d80a...ea6afcd8 is .legion/ only.
